pedagogy.learning_objective: Compute the probability of at least one hit in two independent fixed-probability attempts using the complement of two misses.
prerequisites: Percentages as parts of one hundred
assumptions: The hit probability is fixed at 7/10 in the worked model, and 4/5 in the challenge
The 10×10 grid represents two independent uniform ten-cell axes with seven hit cells each, not an observed 100-attempt sample
limitations: 70 percent is a hypothetical input, not a measured accuracy for any player
A real player may have dependence or changing accuracy, so the model needs validation
At least one includes two hits; it is not exactly one
A probability calculation does not guarantee the outcome of a particular pair of shots
pedagogy.challenge: For two independent attempts at fixed p=0.8, calculate both-miss probability first, then the complement. Pause before revealing the answer.
pedagogy.expected_learning: Explain why 70+70 double-counts both-hit outcomes, and obtain 91 percent for p=0.7 and 96 percent for p=0.8 by subtracting the two-miss chance from one.

sources.title: OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e, 3.2 Independent and Mutually Exclusive Events
sources.locator: Independent Events definition and the complement-event discussion in the two-toss example: P(A)+P(A complement)=1.

sources.title: OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e, 3.3 Two Basic Rules of Probability
sources.locator: The Multiplication Rule for independent events P(A AND B)=P(A)P(B); The Addition Rule P(A OR B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A AND B).

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Expose naive addition producing a value outside the probability range, then pose the correct event.

claims.statement: Probability is bounded by 100 percent; adding the individual hit probabilities without subtracting overlap is invalid.
claims.script_quote: Но вероятность больше ста процентов невозможна!
claims.reasoning: Probability is bounded by 100 percent; adding the individual hit probabilities without subtracting overlap is invalid.
claims.proof: By the probability axioms 0<=P(E)<=1. For hits A and B, union probability is P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B); the both-hit event is counted twice in the naive sum.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: State independence and constant accuracy explicitly, then enumerate all four weighted outcomes.

claims.statement: Independence here means the second hit probability stays 0.7 after either first outcome; this is a stipulated model assumption.
claims.script_quote: Считаем в модели: броски независимы, а точность не меняется. После попадания и после промаха шанс снова забить одинаковый.
claims.reasoning: Independence here means the second hit probability stays 0.7 after either first outcome; this is a stipulated model assumption.

claims.statement: The tree has outcomes PP=49%, PM=21%, MP=21%, MM=9%; these are exhaustive and sum to 100%.
claims.reasoning: The tree has outcomes PP=49%, PM=21%, MP=21%, MM=9%; these are exhaustive and sum to 100%.
claims.proof: Under independence, P(PP)=0.7²=0.49, P(PM)=P(MP)=0.7*0.3=0.21 and P(MM)=0.3²=0.09; 0.49+0.21+0.21+0.09=1. These exact values drive the scene and are checked in tests/test_free_throws.py.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Make the complement event concrete: two misses are the 3×3 red block on an exact 10×10 model grid.

claims.statement: The miss probability is 0.3 per independent attempt; both misses have probability 0.09.
claims.script_quote: Умножаем тридцать сотых на тридцать сотых: девять сотых.
claims.reasoning: The miss probability is 0.3 per independent attempt; both misses have probability 0.09.
claims.proof: Each miss has probability 1-0.7=0.3; independence gives 0.3*0.3=0.09. Each uniform grid axis has 3 miss cells out of10, so both-miss cells number3*3=9 out of100.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Subtract the two-miss probability from one and show that both hits belong to at least one.

claims.statement: The complement of no hits is at least one hit, giving 1-0.09=0.91.
claims.script_quote: Из ста процентов вычитаем девять — получаем девяносто один процент!
claims.reasoning: The complement of no hits is at least one hit, giving 1-0.09=0.91.

claims.statement: At least one contains the both-hit outcome; it is different from exactly one.
claims.reasoning: At least one contains the both-hit outcome; it is different from exactly one.
claims.proof: The event at least one is {PP,PM,MP}; summing its disjoint outcome weights gives0.49+0.21+0.21=0.91. Exactly one would exclude PP.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Transfer the complement method to p=0.8, give thinking time before answer reveal and repeat the model limitation.

claims.statement: Two independent attempts at p=0.8 give both misses0.04 and at least one0.96.
claims.reasoning: Two independent attempts at p=0.8 give both misses0.04 and at least one0.96.

claims.statement: This describes the stipulated probability model, not a guaranteed individual basketball outcome.
claims.script_quote: Это расчёт модели, а не гарантия.
claims.reasoning: This describes the stipulated probability model, not a guaranteed individual basketball outcome.

scientific.scope: Preproduction narration, scene code, probability data and teaching design; playback and pronunciation require separate production QA.

evidence_matches_claims.rationale: OpenStax definitions and product/union rules support the conditional model; the worked numbers follow from explicit inputs without requiring player data.

calculations_correct.rationale: Independent exact-fraction calculation gives49/100,21/100,21/100,9/100; the3x3 miss block leaves91/100. For p=4/5 the result is1-(1/5)^2=24/25.

assumptions_and_limits.rationale: Scene2 specifies constant accuracy and equal second-shot probability after either first result; scene3 labels an equiprobable model grid and scene5 reiterates independence.

no_overclaim.rationale: Accuracy is hypothetical, real-player independence needs checking and the ending distinguishes probability from a guarantee.

pedagogical.scope: Preproduction narration, scene code, probability data and teaching design; playback and pronunciation require separate production QA.

age_and_prerequisites.rationale: The free-throw setting, explicit P/M key and hundred-cell grid support a12-year-old with percentages, decimal multiplication and subtraction.

objective_alignment.rationale: All steps serve the same question: enumerate pairs, count both misses, then take the complement.

explanation_clarity.rationale: Ordered weighted leaves show all four cases; the3x3 red block connects multiplication to counting. The successful list includes PP, explaining why simple addition fails.

challenge_checks_understanding.rationale: Changing accuracy to80 percent requires transfer of the method; a question and hint precede the96 percent answer reveal.
